fixes.explanation: That's the job. The fifty gold clasps join the curtains together, “so that the tabernacle was a unit.” (Exodus 36:13). Two sets of five curtains go in, and one tabernacle comes out. Fifty little gold clasps holding it all together, and I can't even keep my apron strings tied on a humid day.

Six it is. The eleven curtains are joined into one set of five and another of six (Exodus 36:16). Five plus six makes eleven. I counted them off with my mustache, twice, because I don't trust my own math.
Fifty. Each set of goat hair curtains gets fifty loops along its edge (Exodus 36:17). The linen curtains also had fifty loops (Exodus 36:12). Fifty again, so keep that number handy, friend.

Twenty is on the low side. The text says fifty loops along the edge of each set of goat hair curtains (Exodus 36:17). That matches the fifty loops on the linen curtains (Exodus 36:12). That's a whole lot of looping, and I get tired just reading it.

True. The veil is made of blue, purple and scarlet yarn and finely spun linen, with cherubim skillfully worked into it (Exodus 36:35). That's the same list of materials as the ten curtains (Exodus 36:8), with the same skillfully worked cherubim. The veil and the curtains match.

Bronze does show up in this passage, but not under these posts. The veil's four posts stand on cast silver bases (Exodus 36:36). Bronze bases belong to the five posts at the tent's entrance (Exodus 36:38). Silver for the veil, bronze for the door.

Stone doesn't show up under these posts. The text says the five entrance posts stand on bases of bronze (Exodus 36:38). The veil's posts get silver (Exodus 36:36). It's metal all the way down, friend.

A lion isn't what's there. The text says Bezalel makes two cherubim of hammered gold at the ends of the mercy seat (Exodus 37:7). One cherub is on one end and one on the other, all made from one piece of gold (Exodus 37:8). So it's cherubim at both ends.

An eagle isn't the answer here. The text says Bezalel makes two cherubim of hammered gold at the ends of the mercy seat (Exodus 37:7). One cherub is on one end and one on the other, all made from one piece of gold (Exodus 37:8). Cherubim sit at both ends.

True. The cherubim had wings that spread upward, overshadowing the mercy seat, and they faced each other, looking toward the mercy seat (Exodus 37:9). Wings up, faces turned toward the mercy seat. Two gold cherubim, facing each other.

Not quite. The text says, “The buds and branches were all of one piece with the lampstand, hammered out of pure gold.” (Exodus 37:22). So the buds and branches weren't made separately and attached afterward. They're one piece with the lampstand. Hammering all that out of pure gold sounds like a long day, and I'd need a nap.

False is right. The text says, “The buds and branches were all of one piece with the lampstand, hammered out of pure gold.” (Exodus 37:22). So they weren't made separately and attached afterward. They're one piece with the lampstand. I bet that took some arm strength.

Judah. The inventory says Bezalel is of the tribe of Judah (Exodus 38:22). It even gives his family line: son of Uri, the son of Hur. I think that's a proud name to have written next to yours, while all I've got is “Dorin” carved on my handle.

Levi isn't the tribe here. The text says Bezalel is of the tribe of Judah (Exodus 38:22). The Levites show up one verse earlier, as the ones who recorded the inventory under Ithamar son of Aaron the priest (Exodus 38:21). So the Levites kept the records, and Bezalel did the building.

Benjamin isn't the tribe named here. The text says Bezalel is of the tribe of Judah (Exodus 38:22). Notice how much family the inventory gives him: son of Uri, the son of Hur. Only Judah gets attached to his name.

Levi isn't it. The Levites recorded the inventory (Exodus 38:21), but the text says Oholiab son of Ahisamach is of the tribe of Dan (Exodus 38:23). He worked with Bezalel as an engraver, designer and embroiderer. The Levites held the pen, and Oholiab did the stitching.
